pages.title: About — the house
pages.content:
The house

Sazanami Hotel is the timber boathouse at 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren, built in 1934 and opened as a hotel in 2011. Seven rooms stand in one row, and every room faces the water.

The house

The building began as a timber boathouse in 1934 and has stayed on this shore.

In 2011 it was rebuilt as Sazanami Hotel: seven rooms in a single row, each with a window toward Lake Mirren.

A long timber corridor runs the length of the house, with morning light on the floor and a door to each room. There is a small lounge with a wood stove for the evening, when the lake shows dark in the window. Ilse Varga is owner and host. Tomas Reyes, co-owner, is the carpenter who rebuilt the rooms. The notice on the house says that seven rooms face the water, from 1 March. Separately, the house is closed from 6 to 31 January for repairs. In the open months the front desk runs from 7:00 to 22:00, check-in is from 15:00 to 20:00, and check-out is at 11:00. The address is 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren. The desk telephone is +00 555 0140, and the desk email is stay@sazanami-hotel.example.

the people

The people

Seven people look after the house and the neighbours on this stretch of shore. Ilse Varga is owner and host. Tomas Reyes is co-owner and the carpenter who rebuilt the rooms for the opening in 2011. Amara Okafor is the breakfast cook. Jun Park works the front desk, which is open from 7:00 to 22:00. Léa Moreau leads housekeeping and takes the rooms in hand after check-out at 11:00.

Henrik Dahl is a neighbour, not a hotel porter: he keeps the boats at Mirren Boat House, three minutes on foot. Priya Nair is the baker at Harbour Lane Bakery, seven minutes on foot. The house publishes these names with a role and a single duty each. Quiet hours from 22:00 to 7:00, the breakfast hour, and the boat hour all sit with one of these seven. Questions about a stay go to Jun Park’s desk or to stay@sazanami-hotel.example.

a day at Sazanami

A day at Sazanami

The day follows the lake. At 05:30 the light is already on the water. The early breakfast hamper is ready from 6:30 for people taking a boat out, at €18. Breakfast is then served at the window from 7:30 until 10:00, included for the two guests on the room rate. Check-out is at 11:00. Through the afternoon the desk stays open, and new arrivals are received from 15:00 until 20:00. At 22:00 the desk closes and quiet hours begin.

Quiet hours last until 7:00. The lake is the quietest at six. From 6 to 31 January this order stops: the house is closed for repairs, and the rooms are not offered. A rowboat for a half-day is €30, kept with Henrik Dahl at Mirren Boat House. Parking at the hotel holds eight cars. Mirren station is twelve minutes away by the hotel car.

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Rooms

Four room types make up the seven rooms at Sazanami Hotel, and every room faces the water. Rates are per night for two guests, with breakfast included.

Shore Room

The Shore Room is 24 square metres, with a maximum of two guests.

Two rooms are of this type.

The rate is €210 a night for two guests, breakfast included.

The bed is low and dressed in linen, set toward a wide window onto the lake in the morning. The same room type is shown with a deep stone bath beside a tall window, the water outside the glass. Because the maximum is two, the extra bed at €45 belongs to the larger types, where another sleeper still fits the published maximum. Ground-floor rooms 1 and 2 are the rooms to name when a guest needs one level; ask the desk which type they hold for those dates. Check-in is from 15:00 to 20:00, and check-out is at 11:00. Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 7:00 along the whole row.

Window-Seat Room

The Window-Seat Room is 28 square metres, with a maximum of two guests.

Two rooms are of this type.

The rate is €245 a night for two guests, breakfast included.

The bed is for those two guests. Beside it, a window seat with a cushion faces the lake, a linen curtain lifting in a light breeze, the timber sill in the foreground and the far shore beyond. Early light reaches the seat well before the desk opens at 7:00. Breakfast is served at the window from 7:30 to 10:00, so the seat and the table share the same outlook. The early hamper, if you need food before that, is €18 from 6:30 and is requested on the booking, not assumed. Nights on a request may run from 1 to 14. The house replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link.

Corner Lake Room

The Corner Lake Room is 34 square metres, with a maximum of three guests.

Two rooms are of this type.

The rate is €290 a night for two guests, breakfast included.

The room has a bed for those two guests. A third guest uses the extra bed at €45 for the night. The corner holds an armchair, a wool blanket, and a few books, with the lake in the window beside them. Children count toward the maximum of three. The booking form allows one to four guests across the house, and this room still stops at three. Put the total, including children, in the request, and choose Corner Lake Room or any lake room. Check-out is at 11:00. Léa Moreau and housekeeping take the room after that hour. The view is the lake, the same water every room in the row is turned toward.

Jetty Suite

The Jetty Suite is the one large room: 46 square metres, maximum four guests, a single room.

The rate is €380 a night for two guests, breakfast included.

The bed is for those two guests.

Further guests, up to the maximum of four, use extra beds at €45 each night per bed. The room looks toward the mist lifting off the lake, the line of reeds, and the timber jetty. A rowboat for a half-day is €30 and is arranged with Henrik Dahl at Mirren Boat House, three minutes on foot. It is not added to the room rate unless you ask. Arrivals are from 15:00 to 20:00. The rest of a confirmed stay is settled at departure, after the 30 % deposit from the link in the desk’s reply. Free cancellation runs up to 14 days before arrival.

rates

Rates

All rates are in euros, per night, for two guests, with breakfast included. Shore Room: two rooms, 24 square metres, maximum two guests, €210. Window-Seat Room: two rooms, 28 square metres, maximum two guests, €245. Corner Lake Room: two rooms, 34 square metres, maximum three guests, €290. Jetty Suite: one room, 46 square metres, maximum four guests, €380. An extra bed is €45. An early breakfast hamper is €18. A rowboat for a half-day is €30.

These seven figures are the published list. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January. A request is not yet a confirmation. The desk replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link. Free cancellation is available up to 14 days before arrival. After that, the deposit is kept. Write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example with the subject Stay request.

Request these dates →

pages.title: Breakfast
pages.content:
Breakfast

Breakfast is served at your window table from 7:30 to 10:00 and is included for the two guests on the room rate. An early hamper for boats can go out from 6:30.

Times

Breakfast at Sazanami Hotel is 7:30 to 10:00 at your window table.

The early breakfast hamper is from 6:30 for early boats and costs €18.

The window breakfast itself is already included for two guests, so the €18 is only the hamper.

Amara Okafor is the breakfast cook. The front desk opens at 7:00, and Jun Park can note a hamper on the stay if you mark the checkbox on the booking form. Boats leave from the jetty. Henrik Dahl keeps them at Mirren Boat House, three minutes on foot, and a half-day in a rowboat is €30. The lake is the quietest at six, which is the quiet stretch before the hamper. At 05:30 the lake light is already on the water. Quiet hours still run until 7:00, so the early start stays soft. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January, and breakfast is not served in those days.

the table

The four things on the table

Four items make up the window breakfast. First, sliced rye bread. Second, butter and jam. Third, a boiled egg. Fourth, coffee, with the pot on the table and the cup poured there. The table is set in the window: bread, butter, jam, and the coffee pot in the lake light. There is no separate price list for these four, because breakfast is included for the two guests on the rate.

Priya Nair is the baker at Harbour Lane Bakery, seven minutes on foot, for a loaf beyond the table. Vegetarian or gluten-free breakfasts are prepared on request the day before. Say so in the booking message, or write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example the day before arrival, not at the table that morning. The cook’s kitchen is the one kitchen. Room types and nightly rates stay on the rooms page; this table does not change them. Check-out remains 11:00, after the last sitting.

pages.title: Around the lake
pages.content:
Around the lake

From 14 Shore Lane the shore runs past a boat house, a bakery, a loop path, and a cove. Four further names sit on the same list, without a published walking time.

around

Mirren Boat House, the bakery, the trail, the cove

Mirren Boat House is three minutes on foot. Henrik Dahl keeps the boats there. Wooden rowing boats are tied at the house, and a rowboat for a half-day is €30. Harbour Lane Bakery is seven minutes on foot. Priya Nair is the baker, and the window shows loaves on a shelf. The Shore Trail is a 5.2 km loop, a footpath through birch trees along the shore.

Shore Trail Trust is the neighbour name printed with that path. Willow Cove is ten minutes on foot: stone swimming steps into a quiet cove. These four are the distances the hotel publishes. Parking at Sazanami Hotel holds eight cars. Lake Mirren Rowing is named with the other shore marks at the front of the house, beside the boat house, the bakery, and the trail trust. Map and directions from the home page come back to these names on this page.

Four more places are listed with no walking time of their own. The Mirren village shop is the shop in the village. St Aud’s chapel walk is the walk to the chapel. Bicycle hire is at the station. The lake ferry runs in summer. For the train, use the figure the house does give: Mirren station is twelve minutes from the door by the hotel car.

By car, Sazanami Hotel is two hours from the city, then to 14 Shore Lane. Guests who want the hotel car should say so on the stay request and keep the arrival inside check-in, from 15:00 to 20:00. The summer ferry is the way in across the water. A ferry fare is not one of the seven hotel prices. Jun Park at the desk, open from 7:00 to 22:00, can go over the arrival before the day. The desk email is stay@sazanami-hotel.example.

pages.title: Booking
pages.content:
Booking

A stay at Sazanami Hotel starts as a request. The desk replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a link for the 30 % deposit.

Four steps

Booking follows four steps. First, choose dates and a room. Nights may run from 1 to 14, and guests from 1 to 4, inside the maximum for that room. Second, send the request by the form or by email. Third, the house replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link. Fourth, arrive from 15:00; the rest is settled at departure. Check-in continues until 20:00.

The room types on the form are Shore Room, Window-Seat Room, Corner Lake Room, Jetty Suite, or any lake room. The early breakfast hamper, at €18, is a checkbox. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January, and those nights are not offered. If the form is not on the page, use the button Email us your dates. It opens a message to stay@sazanami-hotel.example with the subject Stay request. The desk telephone is +00 555 0140 during desk hours, 7:00 to 22:00.

Rate summary and policies

The rate summary is per night for two guests, breakfast included. Shore Room €210. Window-Seat Room €245. Corner Lake Room €290. Jetty Suite €380. An extra bed is €45. The early breakfast hamper is €18. A rowboat for a half-day is €30.

The 30 % deposit is the payment named in the confirmation reply. Free cancellation runs up to 14 days before arrival. After that, the deposit is kept. The form asks for full name, email, phone, arrival date, nights, guests, room type, the hamper checkbox, a message, and consent. Full name, email, arrival date, nights, guests, and consent are required. Phone, room type, the hamper, and the message can be left if you have nothing to add. Consent links to the privacy note. Sizes are 24, 28, 34, and 46 square metres for Shore, Window-Seat, Corner, and Jetty Suite.

The form and the email fallback

The booking form sits on this page after the policies. It is the request itself, not a charged checkout. When a forms plugin is present, that published form is what you fill in. When it is not, the fallback is the same button the house uses everywhere for dates: Email us your dates, addressed to stay@sazanami-hotel.example, subject Stay request. Write the arrival date, the number of nights from 1 to 14, the number of guests from 1 to 4, and the room you want. Add dietary needs for breakfast the day before you need them: vegetarian or gluten-free.

Add the hamper if you are going out at 6:30. Name children in the guest count. Name an animal in the message so the reply can deal with it. A voucher, if you have one, can be mentioned in the same message. The reply within 24 hours is the confirmation.

pages.title: Stay information
pages.content:
Stay information

These ten notes cover arrival, the people who can stay, the ground floor, parking, quiet hours, closure, payment, and breakfast. Figures match the desk list and do not add a second set of rules.

When is check-in?

Check-in at Sazanami Hotel is from 15:00 to 20:00. The front desk, where Jun Park receives arrivals, is open from 7:00 to 22:00 and closes at 22:00. Plan to be at 14 Shore Lane by 20:00 so the key can be handed over while check-in is still open. If you come by train, the hotel car from Mirren station takes twelve minutes. If you come by car, the drive from the city is two hours.

The summer lake ferry is the other way onto this shore. A stay request is confirmed only when the desk replies, which it does within 24 hours, with a 30 % deposit link. You then arrive from 15:00, and the rest is settled at departure. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January, so those dates have no check-in. The email is stay@sazanami-hotel.example and the phone is +00 555 0140.

When is check-out?

Check-out is at 11:00. Léa Moreau and housekeeping take the rooms after that hour, so the row can be ready for arrivals from 15:00. Breakfast has already finished by then: the window table runs from 7:30 to 10:00. If you are leaving on an early boat, the hamper from 6:30 is the meal to request, at €18, rather than a later table. The desk is open from 7:00, which gives the morning before 11:00 a person at the door.

Quiet hours end at 7:00, so the last part of the night stays hushed even though the desk opens then. The seven rooms are one row, all facing the water, and a late check-out is not a published option on this list. If you need to leave a bag while you walk the 5.2 km Shore Trail, say so to the desk that morning. Phone +00 555 0140.

Can children stay?

Children stay as guests, inside the maximum for the room. Rates are for two guests with breakfast included. The Shore Room and the Window-Seat Room each take a maximum of two guests. The Corner Lake Room takes three. The Jetty Suite takes four. The booking form accepts one to four guests, and the room maximum still applies. An extra bed is €45 a night where that maximum allows another person.

The house does not publish a separate child rate, a separate breakfast price, or an age cutoff. Write the full guest count, children included, and name the room type: Shore Room, Window-Seat Room, Corner Lake Room, Jetty Suite, or any lake room. Quiet hours from 22:00 to 7:00 cover the whole row. Check-in for a family is the same window, 15:00 to 20:00. Send the request to stay@sazanami-hotel.example. The desk replies within 24 hours.

Do you take pets?

A pet charge is not among the seven published prices. Those prices are Shore Room €210, Window-Seat Room €245, Corner Lake Room €290, Jetty Suite €380, extra bed €45, early hamper €18, and rowboat half-day €30. The house is seven rooms in one timber row, with quiet hours from 22:00 to 7:00. If you hope to travel with an animal, write that in the message of the stay request before you treat the dates as settled. The request goes to stay@sazanami-hotel.example with the subject Stay request.

The desk replies within 24 hours, and that reply is where the house accepts or declines the request as written. Jun Park reads desk mail from 7:00 to 22:00. The confirmation, together with the 30 % deposit link, is the record of what was agreed. The lake path and the jetty do not by themselves decide the question.

Which rooms are on the ground floor?

Ground-floor rooms are rooms 1 and 2. They are the rooms to ask for when stairs are a problem. The hotel does not publish a lift, a step count, or a turning radius, so this page will not invent those measurements. What it can say is plain: the house is one row of seven rooms, rebuilt in 2011 from the 1934 boathouse, with a long timber corridor and a door to each room. Tell the desk you need a ground-floor room, and say whether room 1 or room 2 is required, or either.

Also name the type if you know it, and the number of guests. Maxima remain two, two, three, or four depending on Shore, Window-Seat, Corner, and Jetty Suite. Check-in is 15:00 to 20:00. Write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example or call +00 555 0140 between 7:00 and 22:00. Parking for eight cars is on the property.

Is there parking, and for how many cars?

Parking at the hotel holds eight cars. No parking fee appears on the rate list, and this page does not add one. The eight spaces sit with the house at 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren. By car, the drive from the city is two hours. If the eight spaces matter for your arrival, say how many cars you are bringing when you request the stay, inside the message to stay@sazanami-hotel.example.

Check-in is still 15:00 to 20:00, and the desk is open from 7:00 to 22:00. Guests coming by train can use the hotel car from Mirren station, twelve minutes, and then do without a parking space. The summer ferry is the other arrival that does not need a car. Mirren Boat House is three minutes on foot and Harbour Lane Bakery is seven minutes, so some days the car can stay put. The Shore Trail is a 5.2 km loop from the door.

What are the quiet hours?

Quiet hours are from 22:00 to 7:00. They cover every room in the row of seven. At 22:00 the front desk also closes, so the start of quiet hours and the end of the desk day are the same moment. The desk opens again at 7:00, which is when quiet hours end. Breakfast at the window begins at 7:30, after that change. The early hamper from 6:30 falls inside quiet hours and is meant for people already going out to a boat, not for a loud send-off.

The lake is the quietest at six. At 05:30 the light is on the water and the house is still in the quiet period. If you need the desk before 7:00, the published hours do not offer it. Call +00 555 0140 from 7:00, or write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example and the reply will come within 24 hours for a stay request. Check-in never starts before 15:00.

When is the house closed?

Sazanami Hotel is closed from 6 to 31 January for repairs. Those dates cannot be booked, and the desk does not receive arrivals then. The notice on the house, separate from that closure, says that seven rooms face the water, from 1 March. Tomas Reyes, co-owner and the carpenter who rebuilt the rooms in 2011, is the person tied to the timber of the house. The closure is the repair period the hotel publishes.

It is not a rate season and it does not create a winter price. Outside those January dates, check-in is 15:00 to 20:00, check-out is 11:00, the desk is 7:00 to 22:00, and breakfast is 7:30 to 10:00. Stay requests for open dates still receive a reply within 24 hours, with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link. Email stay@sazanami-hotel.example with the subject Stay request. The address remains 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren, including in the closed weeks.

How do the deposit and cancellation work?

The booking has four steps. You choose dates and a room, then send the request by form or email. The house replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link. You arrive from 15:00, and the rest is settled at departure. Free cancellation runs up to 14 days before arrival. After that, the deposit is kept. The nightly rates this deposit refers to, for two guests with breakfast, are Shore Room €210, Window-Seat Room €245, Corner Lake Room €290, and Jetty Suite €380.

An extra bed is €45, the early hamper is €18, and a rowboat half-day is €30, if you add them. Nights run from 1 to 14. Guests run from 1 to 4, inside the room maximum. The house is closed 6 to 31 January. The mail address is stay@sazanami-hotel.example and the subject for dates is Stay request. Phone +00 555 0140 during desk hours.

When is breakfast, and can the kitchen change it?

Breakfast is from 7:30 to 10:00 at your window table and is included for the two guests covered by the room rate. The early breakfast hamper is from 6:30 for early boats and costs €18. Amara Okafor is the breakfast cook. The four items on the table are sliced rye bread, butter and jam, a boiled egg, and coffee. Vegetarian or gluten-free breakfasts are made on request the day before. Put that request in the booking message, or email stay@sazanami-hotel.example the day before you need it.

The hamper checkbox on the booking form is how you ask for the 6:30 basket. Breakfast is not served from 6 to 31 January, when the house is closed. Priya Nair bakes at Harbour Lane Bakery, seven minutes on foot, if you want bread beyond the table. Quiet hours end at 7:00, and the first window sitting follows at 7:30. Check-out is at 11:00, after the service has ended.

pages.title: Newsletter
pages.content:
Newsletter

A short letter leaves Sazanami Hotel four times a year. It is called a letter from the lake, and it starts only when you send the message yourself.

A letter from the lake

The letter is a note from 14 Shore Lane, four times a year, about the lake, the window breakfast, and the season the house is in.

It does not hold a room and it does not take the place of a confirmation.

The January letter falls while the house is closed, from 6 to 31 January, for repairs. Other letters belong to the open months: the light at 05:30, breakfast from 7:30 to 10:00, the jetty, and the neighbours. Henrik Dahl keeps the boats at Mirren Boat House, three minutes on foot. Priya Nair bakes at Harbour Lane Bakery, seven minutes on foot. Ilse Varga is owner and host. The Shore Trail, when a letter mentions a walk, is the 5.2 km loop. Willow Cove is the swimming steps, ten minutes on foot. Rates, when a letter needs them, stay the published ones, beginning at €210 for the Shore Room.

How the form works

The form asks for your email. The button reads Send me the letter. The subject of the message is Letter from the lake. The address is stay@sazanami-hotel.example. The notice under the form reads: Opens your email app. Send the message to receive the letter from the lake; you are not subscribed yet. The page will not say that you have joined a list.

You are subscribed only in the sense the notice allows: after you send the message. If no mail plugin is active, the form opens your email app with the address you typed and that same warning. You may also write from the contact page. That button reads Write to the desk, with the subject A question for the desk. The letter remains four times a year. A stay is still a separate request, with a reply within 24 hours and a 30 % deposit link.

pages.title: Contact and access
pages.content:
Contact and access

The desk of Sazanami Hotel is at 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren. Call +00 555 0140 or write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example while the desk is open.

Address, hours, phone, email

The address is 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren.

The front desk is open from 7:00 to 22:00.

Check-in is from 15:00 to 20:00. Check-out is at 11:00. Quiet hours are 22:00 to 7:00. Jun Park works the desk. Ilse Varga is owner and host. For a stay, the mail subject is Stay request and the button reads Email us your dates. For any other question, the button reads Write to the desk and the subject is A question for the desk. The contact form asks for name, email, subject, message, and consent. Name, email, message, and consent are required. Both kinds of message use stay@sazanami-hotel.example. The telephone is +00 555 0140. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January for repairs, and the desk does not take arrivals on those dates. Parking on the property holds eight cars. Seven rooms face the water.

getting here

By car, by train, by lake ferry

By car, the hotel is two hours from the city, and the last turn is into 14 Shore Lane. Parking holds eight cars. By train, come to Mirren station and take the hotel car, twelve minutes to the door. Ask for that car in your message, and keep the arrival inside check-in, 15:00 to 20:00. By lake ferry, the crossing runs in summer and reaches this shore. The timber jetty in front of the house runs into flat water.

Mirren Boat House, where Henrik Dahl keeps the boats, is three minutes on foot. A ferry fare is not on the hotel rate list. The seven published prices are the four rooms, the extra bed at €45, the hamper at €18, and the half-day rowboat at €30. After arrival, breakfast is at the window from 7:30 to 10:00. The early hamper, if you requested it, is from 6:30. The contact form is on this page for anything the clock does not answer.

pages.title: Gift a stay
pages.content:
Gift a stay

A stay at Sazanami Hotel can be given as a voucher, ordered by email. There is no shop, no cart, and no checkout on this page.

Voucher amounts

You may name the voucher as €100, as €245, or as any amount you choose.

€245 is the same figure as one night in the Window-Seat Room for two guests with breakfast included.

The nightly rates begin at €210 for the Shore Room, so a €100 voucher is a sum toward a stay, not a whole night at a published rate. Any other amount is the sum you write in the email. The Corner Lake Room is €290 a night and the Jetty Suite is €380, both for two guests with breakfast. An extra bed is €45, the early hamper is €18, and a rowboat half-day is €30. Those remain hotel prices, not extra voucher denominations. The house will take €100, €245, or the amount you set. Order by email to stay@sazanami-hotel.example. The photograph of the evening lounge is only a picture of the house, not a voucher design you must choose.

how to order

How to order

Write to stay@sazanami-hotel.example and say that you want to give a stay. Include the amount, €100, €245, or any other sum, and the recipient’s name. If you want the note to mention a room, use the published names only: Shore Room, Window-Seat Room, Corner Lake Room, Jetty Suite, or any lake room. A voucher is not a confirmed reservation. The person who receives it still chooses dates and sends a stay request. The four steps still apply: choose dates and a room, send the request, receive a reply within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link, then arrive from 15:00.

The rest is settled at departure. Free cancellation runs up to 14 days before arrival. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January. There is no shop page to add the voucher to a basket. The desk telephone is +00 555 0140.

Email the desk about a voucher

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

This note says what Sazanami Hotel collects when you request a stay, write to the desk, or ask for the letter from the lake. It covers the forms on this site and the mailbox stay@sazanami-hotel.example.

Stay requests and desk messages

Stay requests and desk messages go to stay@sazanami-hotel.example. A stay request may include full name, email, phone, arrival date, nights from 1 to 14, guests from 1 to 4, a room type, the early breakfast hamper checkbox, a message, and consent. Full name, email, arrival date, nights, guests, and consent are required. Phone, room type, the hamper, and the message are optional. Room types are Shore Room, Window-Seat Room, Corner Lake Room, Jetty Suite, and any lake room. A contact message may include name, email, subject, message, and consent. Name, email, message, and consent are required there. The contact subject is A question for the desk.

The booking subject is Stay request. The button for dates reads Email us your dates. The button for other questions reads Write to the desk. The telephone is +00 555 0140. The address is 14 Shore Lane, Lake Mirren. Jun Park works the desk from 7:00 to 22:00. Ilse Varga is owner and host.

The letter, gifts, and corrections

The letter from the lake is sent four times a year. The form asks for an email address. The button reads Send me the letter. The mail subject is Letter from the lake. The notice on the form says: Opens your email app. Send the message to receive the letter from the lake; you are not subscribed yet. Until you send that message, the house does not treat you as subscribed. Consent on the stay form and the contact form points to this page.

Gift vouchers of €100, €245, or any amount are ordered by email to the same address. There is no shop account. If a line in a message is wrong, write again to stay@sazanami-hotel.example and say what to correct. The published reply to a stay request is within 24 hours. The house is closed from 6 to 31 January, and those dates are not booked. Desk hours in the open months are 7:00 to 22:00. This page does not set a retention period in days, because the house has not published one.

categories.name: From the lake
categories.description: Notes from the house and the shore.

posts.title: The first hour on the water
posts.excerpt: Before breakfast, the jetty at Sazanami Hotel is a quiet timber line into Lake Mirren, and the first hour belongs to mist, one rowboat, and the light at 05:30.
posts.content:
The first hour on the water is the hour the house leaves empty on purpose. At 05:30 the lake light is already on the timber at 14 Shore Lane. The seven rooms are still a row of closed doors. Check-out is not until 11:00, and the front desk does not open until 7:00. If you step outside, the sound is water at the piles and your own feet on the boards.

By 05:40 the jetty is the clearest line on the shore. It is a narrow timber walk into flat water, mist on the lake, the sun still low. From the end of it a single rowboat sits in the fog. If someone is in the boat, you see them from behind, already turned toward the far shore. The hotel publishes one figure for this, and only one: a rowboat for a half-day is €30. Henrik Dahl keeps the boats. He is the neighbour at Mirren Boat House, three minutes on foot, not a guide hired by the hour.

Sazanami Hotel was a timber boathouse built in 1934. It opened as a hotel in 2011, after Tomas Reyes, co-owner and carpenter, rebuilt the rooms. Ilse Varga is owner and host. The plan they kept is small. Seven rooms stand in one row, and every room faces the water. You do not cross a road to see the lake. You lift the curtain. In a Window-Seat Room the linen moves a little, the sill is pale timber, and the far shore sits in the early light. The Jetty Suite, the one room of 46 square metres, looks toward the same mist and the same reeds. Shore Rooms are 24 square metres. Window-Seat Rooms are 28 square metres. Corner Lake Rooms are 34 square metres. The view is shared. The size is the difference. Each type has a bed for the two guests on the rate, and the larger rooms can add the extra bed at €45 up to their own maximum.

People who want to be on the water before the window service ask for the early hamper. It is ready from 6:30 and it costs €18. It is for early boats. Breakfast itself is included for the two guests on the room rate and is served at the window from 7:30 to 10:00. Amara Okafor is the breakfast cook. On the table are sliced rye bread, butter and jam, a boiled egg, and coffee. Between the hamper and that table there is a short quiet stretch. Before the hamper is the hour this piece describes. The lake is the quietest at six. Quiet hours run from 22:00 to 7:00, so six in the morning still belongs to them. The mist has started to thin. The reeds show as a line. The desk is not open yet.

Jun Park opens the desk at 7:00. Léa Moreau’s housekeeping follows the rooms through the late morning, after check-out at 11:00. The long timber corridor, the row of doors, and the light on the floor belong to those later hours, when people are actually leaving or arriving. Arrivals are from 15:00 to 20:00. Come by train and Mirren station is twelve minutes by the hotel car. Come by road and the drive from the city is two hours. Come by the lake ferry and the crossing is a summer one. However you arrived, the jetty the next morning is the same jetty. Parking, if you brought a car, holds eight cars.

A walk can wait until after breakfast. The Shore Trail is a 5.2 km loop through birch trees along the shore, and Shore Trail Trust is the name beside that path. Willow Cove, with the stone swimming steps, is ten minutes on foot. Harbour Lane Bakery, where Priya Nair bakes, is seven minutes. Lake Mirren Rowing sits among the neighbour names at the front of the house. None of those walks is the first hour. The first hour is the jetty, the fog, and the choice to push off or to go back to the window seat until the coffee is poured.

The house is closed from 6 to 31 January for repairs. The rooms are not offered, and the desk is not receiving guests. There is no stay to put on the water in those weeks. Tomas Reyes’s care of the timber belongs to that closure. Henrik Dahl’s care of the boats continues at Mirren Boat House next door. The notice on the house, in its own words, says that seven rooms face the water, from 1 March. For the months when the desk is open, the way onto the lake does not change.

You book by request. Choose dates and a room. Nights run from 1 to 14. Guests run from 1 to 4, and never above the room’s maximum: two in a Shore Room or a Window-Seat Room, three in a Corner Lake Room, four in the Jetty Suite. Send the form, or email stay@sazanami-hotel.example with the subject Stay request. The desk replies within 24 hours with a confirmation and a 30 % deposit link. You arrive from 15:00. The rest is settled when you leave. Free cancellation runs up to 14 days before arrival. After that, the deposit is kept. The nightly rates for two guests, breakfast included, are €210, €245, €290, and €380.

If you remember one clock, remember the morning. Be on the jetty around 05:40 if the first light is why you came. Ask for the hamper when you book if you want food before 7:30. Otherwise wait for the window table from 7:30. The water was here when the boathouse went up in 1934, and it is the water the seven rooms were turned toward in 2011. Phone the desk on +00 555 0140 between 7:00 and 22:00 if the morning plan needs a person rather than a letter.

posts.title: Why breakfast is served at the window
posts.excerpt: There is no breakfast room at Sazanami Hotel. The table comes to your window, and the reasons are practical as well as pleasant.
posts.content:
There is no breakfast room at Sazanami Hotel. When the house was rebuilt in 2011, Tomas Reyes and Ilse Varga talked for a long time about where breakfast should happen, and every plan that put guests in one room, facing one another, took something from the view. The rooms already had the lake. So the table goes to the window.

From 7:30 to 10:00, Amara Okafor sends out a table to each room that asks for one: bread from Harbour Lane Bakery, where Priya Nair bakes before dawn, butter, jam, a boiled egg and a pot of coffee. The table is set against the glass, so the lake sits just beyond the plate. It is a small thing, but it changes the meal. Nobody hurries.

There are practical reasons too. Seven rooms is a small house, and a tray at the door is simpler than a dining room that is empty for most of the day. The kitchen can work calmly, one table after another, and a guest who wakes late is not behind anyone. A guest who needs a vegetarian or gluten-free plate only has to tell us the day before.

For anyone who wants to be on the water early, there is a hamper from 6:30 for €18, packed for a rowboat or the Shore Trail. It holds the same things as the table, in a form that travels.

Most mornings the table is cleared by eleven, in time for check-out, and the cushions on the window seats are turned over for the next guest. We think of the window as the house's one real dining room, and it happens to have seven sides.

posts.title: What we mend in January
posts.excerpt: The house closes from 6 to 31 January for repairs. What gets mended while the lake is quiet, and who does it.
posts.content:
Sazanami Hotel closes every year from 6 to 31 January. The lake is at its stillest then, often with a rim of ice along the reeds, and the house gets the attention that the busy months do not allow.

Most of the work is timber. The boathouse was built in 1934, and the jetty and the corridor floor take the weather and a great many footsteps. Tomas Reyes, who rebuilt the rooms and is a carpenter by trade, goes through every room with a plane and a tin of oil. He checks the window seats first, because the sills carry the most weight and the most light.

Léa Moreau washes the linen curtains and turns the mattresses. Amara Okafor reorders the kitchen and tries new bread with Priya Nair at Harbour Lane Bakery, a few of which reach the breakfast table in the spring. Jun Park repaints the small things the desk sees all year, from the key rack to the register.

The wood stove in the lounge is swept and tested before the first cold evening, and the chimney is checked. It is the one fire in the house, and we like it to be reliable.

Henrik Dahl, who keeps the boats at Mirren Boat House, brings the rowboats up onto the shore and repairs them for the season. By 1 February the house has been mended where it needed it, the rooms are aired and the first guests of the year arrive to find everything as it was, with one more winter's worth of care in it.
